# Friends Of Appropriate Ages

## Problem

## Requirements

You are given an integer array `ages[]`. Compute the overall number of friend requests that are made. A person `A` may send a request to person `B` only when all of these statements are false:

- `age[B] <= 0.5 * age[A] + 7`
- `age[B] > age[A]`
- `age[B] > 100 && age[A] < 100`

Keep in mind that if every age lies in `[1, 120]`, the third test already follows from the first two tests and can generally be omitted.

When two distinct people are eligible to send requests in both directions, they contribute 2 requests. A person cannot send a request to themselves.

Function signature:

```
int numFriendRequests(int[] ages)
```

## Examples

```
ages = [15,15] -> 2
```

Both 15-year-olds can request the other person, so there are two directed requests.

```
ages = [17,18,19] -> 3
```

The 18-year-old can request the 17-year-old, and the 19-year-old can request both the 17-year-old and the 18-year-old.

```
ages = [21,31,99,109,119] -> 3
```

The 109-year-old can request the 99-year-old, and the 119-year-old can request both the 109-year-old and the 99-year-old. The 31-year-old cannot request the 21-year-old because `21 <= 0.5 * 31 + 7`.


## Notes

## Preparation

- Before coding, work through why the third rule becomes unnecessary when ages are limited to 120.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Reframe the condition as: A can send a request to B only if B's age is in (0.5*A + 7, A] (or (,A] with upper bound), essentially a range check.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a frequency array for ages (since ages are bounded by 120) and prefix sums to quickly count how many people fall in the allowed range for each age.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The complexity target is O(n + max_age) by iterating over ages and using cumulative counts, avoiding nested loops.

</details>
